title: Count words
description: Count the number of words in a String using the split() method. The separator is the blank space.
hints: Use texto.split(" ") to get an array of words
The resulting array has one word per position
solutionExplanation: The split(" ") method divides the String into an array using the space as the separator. The number of elements in the array corresponds to the number of words.

title: Capitalize title
description: Given a String in lowercase, capitalize the first letter of each word to form a title. Example: 'hola mundo java' → 'Hola Mundo Java'.
hints: Use substring(0,1).toUpperCase() for the first letter
Use substring(1) for the rest of the word
Use String.join(" ", palabras) to rebuild the text
solutionExplanation: The text is split into words with split(). For each word, the first letter is taken with substring(0,1), converted to uppercase with toUpperCase(), and joined with the rest of the word (substring(1)). StringBuilder is used to build the result efficiently.

title: Reverse words
description: Reverse the order of the words in a String without using Collections.reverse(). Example: 'uno dos tres' → 'tres dos uno'.
hints: Create a String array with split(" ")
Swap palabras[i] with palabras[j] using temp
Use String.join(" ", palabras) to join again
solutionExplanation: The text is split into an array of words. Elements are swapped using two indexes from the ends toward the center (the same algorithm used to reverse an array). Finally String.join() is used to rebuild the String with the words in reverse order.
